human.problem: Several story cards retell Isaiah's future prophecy in the present tense, as if it is happening now: "It blooms profusely" (card 4), "The mute tongue shouts for joy... the parched ground becomes a pool" (card 13) and "They come in crowned with everlasting joy" (card 20). The BSB says "will" throughout. The choice cards keep "will." No rule clearly says whether storyteller present tense is allowed for prophecy.
human.question: In prophetic passages, may Papa Dorin retell future promises in the present tense as a storyteller would, or must story cards keep the text's future tense ("will") so the baker doesn't read the prophecy as something already happening?
